content.intro: This lesson covers Filtering with Where-Object in the PowerShell learning path. It expands the supplied syllabus heading into an actionable draft with a visual, a worked example, and a short knowledge check.
content.why_it_matters: PowerShell cmdlets pass objects through the pipeline. Filter early with `Where-Object`, select the properties you need, and sort or group records before exporting or formatting them. Native executables may instead emit text, so do not assume every pipeline has the same object semantics.

content_blocks.code:
$records = @([pscustomobject]@{ Name = 'Mira'; Score = 92 }, [pscustomobject]@{ Name = 'Avi'; Score = 85 }, [pscustomobject]@{ Name = 'Noor'; Score = 67 })
$records | Where-Object { $_.Score -ge 80 } | Sort-Object Score -Descending | Select-Object Name, Score
